main_text.p: adnotarunt & amplexi sunt, qui eas cum Græcis, Hebraicis, Syriacis & Chaldaicis codicibus comparârunt, edisserunt convenientioresque aliquando textui sacro χ[?] ἐμφατικωτέρας quàm sit eo loco vulgatæ textus, multitudine sane obruere-tur; satis erit unius aut alterius, qui hanc quæstione excusserunt, testimonium producere. Sixtus Senensis in postrema Pag.† Bibliothecæ suæ fatetur in vulgata non-nullas inveniri mendas, &c. Postea docet hæc omnia nec fidem nec bonos mores lædere, causasque explicat, ob quas errores & mendas in Scripturis Ecclesia patiatur. Melchior Canus lib. 2. Locorū Theologi, in fine cap. 14. & toto cap. 15. docet utiliter ad fontes sæpe recurri. Inter eas quinta utilitas est ejusmodi, ut mendæ, quæ in vulg. irrepserunt, fontium ope corrigan-tur, quod multis exemplis demonstrat; idem argum. fusè prosequitur lib. II. c. 5. resp. ad argum. 11. & 12, &c. Joannes Mariana in opusculo de editione vulgata c. 21. sic interpretatur Concilii Tridentini decretum, Vulgatæ editionis vitia non

page.notes: Running head is printed as "Jo. MORINUS" with small-capital letters; transcribed in normal case. The "Pag.†" after "postrema" is a printed reference mark with no marginal text on this page. The Greek before "ἐμφατικωτέρας" is doubtful and marked [?]. The printed line break "obruere / tur;" shows no visible hyphen; I wrote it with a hyphen, which may not be printed. The word "non" at the bottom right is the catchword. Printed "Melchior Canus" and "Concilii Tridentini" are spaced as in the scan.
